name: Bismuth Subsalicylate

fields.mechanism_of_action: Bismuth subsalicylate is a fine, white, odorless and tasteless powder that is stable and non-hygroscopic, and is a highly insoluble salt of trivalent bismuth and salicylic acid (bismuth subsalicylate is 2-hydroxybenzoic acid bismuth (3+) salt, molecular weight 362.11); each pink chewable tablet in the prescription kit contains 262.4 mg bismuth subsalicylate, equivalent to 102 mg salicylate (Bismuth Subsalicylate Chewable Tablets/Metronidazole Tablets/Tetracycline Hydrochloride Capsules label, DESCRIPTION). Upon oral administration, bismuth subsalicylate is almost completely hydrolysed in the gastrointestinal tract to bismuth and salicylic acid, so the pharmacokinetics of bismuth subsalicylate are described by the individual pharmacokinetics of bismuth and salicylic acid (same label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY). The antibacterial action of bismuth salts is not well understood (same label, Microbiology, Mechanism of Action); in the Helicobacter pylori regimen the bismuth subsalicylate component is used together with metronidazole and tetracycline as part of combination therapy, and the label states that the combination has been shown to be active against most isolates of Helicobacter pylori both in vitro and in clinical infections (same label, Microbiology and INDICATIONS AND USAGE).
indications: OTC Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets (bismuth subsalicylate 262 mg per chewable tablet) and Pepto-Bismol liquid (bismuth subsalicylate 525 mg per 30 mL dose): purpose stated as upset stomach reliever and antidiarrheal; uses are relief of travellers' diarrhoea, diarrhoea, and upset stomach due to overindulgence in food and drink, including heartburn, indigestion, nausea, gas, belching and fullness (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Purpose and Uses; Pepto-Bismol liquid OTC label, Drug Facts, Purpose and Uses).

Prescription Bismuth Subsalicylate Chewable Tablets/Metronidazole Tablets/Tetracycline Hydrochloride Capsules: the components, in combination with an H2 antagonist, are indicated for the eradication of H. pylori for treatment of patients with H. pylori infection and duodenal ulcer disease (active or a history of duodenal ulcer); eradication of H. pylori has been demonstrated to reduce the risk of duodenal ulcer recurrence in patients with active duodenal ulcer disease (prescription kit label, INDICATIONS AND USAGE).

Bismuth subsalicylate is not listed in the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (23rd List, 2023) or in the Kenya Essential Medicines List 2023 (WHO eEML 23rd List, 2023; KEML 2023); in Kenya, bismuth appears in the list only in the context of heavy-metal poisoning (chelation antidote indications), not as bismuth subsalicylate (KEML 2023, footnote 76).
contraindications: OTC: allergy alert - contains salicylate; do not take if you are allergic to salicylates (including aspirin) or are taking other salicylate products (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).
OTC: do not use if you have an ulcer, a bleeding problem, or bloody or black stool (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).

OTC: do not use in children and teenagers who have or are recovering from chicken pox or flu-like symptoms, because of the risk of Reye's syndrome (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).

Prescription kit: known hypersensitivity (for example urticaria, erythematous rash, flushing and fever) to bismuth subsalicylate, metronidazole or other nitroimidazole derivatives, or tetracycline (prescription kit label, CONTRAINDICATIONS).
Prescription kit: should not be administered to patients with a known allergy to aspirin or other salicylates (prescription kit label, CONTRAINDICATIONS).

Prescription kit: contraindicated in patients with severe renal impairment, and in patients who have taken disulfiram within the last two weeks; methoxyflurane must not be administered to patients taking the product, and alcoholic beverages or products containing propylene glycol must not be consumed during and for at least 3 days after use. The renal impairment, disulfiram, methoxyflurane and alcohol statements relate to the tetracycline and metronidazole components of the kit (prescription kit label, CONTRAINDICATIONS).
side_effects: A temporary, but harmless, darkening of the stool and/or tongue may occur (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings; Pepto-Bismol liquid OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).
Stop use and ask a doctor if ringing in the ears or loss of hearing occurs, or if diarrhoea lasts more than 2 days (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).

Prescription kit, clinical-trial adverse reactions reported in at least 1% of 266 patients: nausea 12.0%, diarrhoea 6.8%, abdominal pain 6.8%, melena 3.0%, upper respiratory infection 2.3%, constipation 1.9%, anorexia 1.5%, asthenia 1.5%, vomiting 1.5%, discoloured tongue 1.5%, headache 1.5%, dyspepsia 1.5%, dizziness 1.5%, stool abnormality (black or dark stools) 1.1%, duodenal ulcer 1.1%, sinusitis 1.1%, taste perversion 1.1%, flatulence 1.1%, gastrointestinal haemorrhage 1.1%, pain 1.1%, insomnia 1.1%, anal discomfort 1.1% and paraesthesia 1.1% (prescription kit label, ADVERSE REACTIONS, Table 1).

Prescription kit, additional adverse reactions reported in under 1% include dry mouth, dysphagia, eructation, GI monilia, glossitis, intestinal obstruction, rectal haemorrhage and stomatitis (gastrointestinal), acne, ecchymosis, photosensitivity reaction, pruritus and rash (skin), cerebral ischaemia, chest pain, hypertension and myocardial infarction (cardiovascular), nervousness and somnolence (CNS), arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and tendonitis (musculoskeletal), and SGOT/SGPT increases (metabolic) (prescription kit label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Prescription kit: skin and subcutaneous disorders including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis and DRESS syndrome have been reported; discontinue treatment at the first evidence of a cutaneous reaction (prescription kit label, WARNINGS). The Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis and DRESS statements relate to the metronidazole and tetracycline components of the combination (prescription kit label, WARNINGS).

dosage.adult: OTC Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets (bismuth subsalicylate 262 mg per tablet): adults and children 12 years and over take 2 chewable tablets every half hour or 4 chewable tablets every hour as needed for diarrhoea, and 2 chewable tablets every half hour to 1 hour as needed for overindulgence (upset stomach, heartburn, indigestion, nausea); do not exceed 8 doses (16 chewable tablets) in 24 hours; use until diarrhoea stops but not more than 2 days; drink plenty of clear fluids to help prevent dehydration caused by diarrhoea (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Directions). OTC Pepto-Bismol liquid (bismuth subsalicylate 525 mg per 30 mL): shake well, use only the dose cup provided, 30 mL every half hour or 60 mL every hour as needed for diarrhoea/travelers' diarrhoea and 30 mL every half hour as needed for overindulgence; do not exceed 8 doses (240 mL) in 24 hours; use until diarrhoea stops but not more than 2 days (Pepto-Bismol liquid OTC label, Drug Facts, Directions). Prescription H. pylori regimen: bismuth subsalicylate 525 mg (two 262.4 mg chewable tablets), metronidazole 250 mg (one tablet) and tetracycline hydrochloride 500 mg (one capsule) taken four times daily for 14 days plus an H2 antagonist approved for the treatment of acute duodenal ulcer; the medicines are taken at mealtimes and at bedtime, the bismuth subsalicylate tablets are chewed and swallowed, and the metronidazole tablet and tetracycline capsule are swallowed whole with a full glass of water (prescription kit label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).
dosage.geriatric: No geriatric-specific dose or dose adjustment is stated in the OTC labelling or in the prescription kit label used. The OTC directions simply apply to adults and children 12 years and over, and the prescription kit regimen is stated for adults, with a note that care should be taken in dose selection in patients with impaired renal function (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Directions; prescription kit label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION and PRECAUTIONS).
dosage.paediatric: OTC: children under 12 years should ask a doctor before using Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets or the Pepto-Bismol liquid (both OTC labels, Drug Facts, Directions). The product must not be used in children and teenagers who have or are recovering from chicken pox or flu-like symptoms because of the risk of Reye's syndrome, and changes in behaviour with nausea and vomiting during use should prompt consultation with a doctor because these symptoms could be an early sign of Reye's syndrome (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).

interactions: Anticoagulants: ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if you are taking any drug for anticoagulation (thinning the blood), and in the prescription kit the combination may alter the anticoagulant effects of warfarin and other oral coumarin anticoagulants; salicylates may cause an increased risk of bleeding when administered with anticoagulant therapy, and prothrombin time, INR or other suitable anticoagulation tests should be closely monitored if the product is administered concomitantly with warfarin (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings; prescription kit label, DRUG INTERACTIONS, Anticoagulants).

Aspirin and other salicylates: the OTC label warns against taking the product if you are allergic to salicylates including aspirin or while taking other salicylate products, and the prescription kit cautions that concomitant aspirin may increase the risk of salicylate toxicity (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings; prescription kit label, DRUG INTERACTIONS).

Antidiabetic agents: caution is advised in the administration of bismuth subsalicylate to patients taking medication for diabetes, because of a possible enhanced hypoglycemic effect when given with salicylates; the OTC label also lists diabetes among the conditions for which a doctor or pharmacist should be consulted before use (prescription kit label, DRUG INTERACTIONS; Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).
Probenecid or sulfinpyrazone: caution is advised, since the uricosuric effects of probenecid or sulfinpyrazone may be decreased (prescription kit label, DRUG INTERACTIONS).
Medicines for gout: the OTC label directs the user to ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if taking any drug for gout (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).

Antacids, multivitamins or dairy products: absorption of the prescription kit may be reduced if administered with antacids containing aluminium, calcium or magnesium, with preparations containing iron, zinc or sodium bicarbonate, or with milk or dairy products (this interaction is attributed to the tetracycline component) (prescription kit label, DRUG INTERACTIONS).
Radiographic procedures: bismuth absorbs x-rays and may interfere with x-ray diagnostic procedures of the gastrointestinal tract (prescription kit label, PRECAUTIONS, Laboratory Test Interactions).

Other interactions in the prescription kit (methoxyflurane, disulfiram, alcohol and propylene glycol, oral contraceptives, lithium, busulfan, cimetidine, phenytoin and phenobarbital) arise from the tetracycline and metronidazole components of the combination, not from bismuth subsalicylate (prescription kit label, CONTRAINDICATIONS and DRUG INTERACTIONS).
fields.monitoring: Stool and tongue darkening is expected, temporary and harmless, but must not be confused with melena, and the patient should be asked to report melena (prescription kit label, PRECAUTIONS, Darkening of the Tongue and/or Black Stool; OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings). Prothrombin time, INR or other suitable anticoagulation tests should be closely monitored if the product is given with warfarin or other oral coumarin anticoagulants (prescription kit label, DRUG INTERACTIONS, Anticoagulants). The appearance of abnormal neurologic signs and symptoms demands prompt evaluation of the benefit/risk ratio of continuing therapy, because cases of neurotoxicity associated with excessive doses of bismuth-containing products, including bismuth subsalicylate, have been reported (prescription kit label, WARNINGS, Bismuth-containing products). Because bismuth subsalicylate may cause salicylate toxicity, tinnitus or hearing loss should be reported and the product stopped (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings). Duration of self-treatment is limited: diarrhoea should not be treated for more than 2 days without medical review (both OTC labels, Drug Facts, Directions and Warnings).
fields.patient_counselling: Fully chew the chewable tablets before swallowing (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Directions); shake the liquid well before use and use only the dose cup provided (Pepto-Bismol liquid OTC label, Drug Facts, Directions). For diarrhoea, use until diarrhoea stops but not more than 2 days; do not exceed 8 doses in 24 hours (16 chewable tablets or 240 mL of liquid) (both OTC labels, Drug Facts, Directions). Drink plenty of clear fluids to help prevent dehydration caused by diarrhoea (both OTC labels, Drug Facts, Directions). Expect a temporary, harmless darkening of the stool and/or tongue; this is not the same as a black, tarry stool from bleeding, and if there is bloody or black stool, do not use the product (both OTC labels, Drug Facts, Warnings). Stop use and ask a doctor if symptoms get worse or last more than 2 days, if ringing in the ears or loss of hearing occurs, or if diarrhoea lasts more than 2 days (both OTC labels, Drug Facts, Warnings). Children and teenagers with chicken pox or flu-like symptoms must not use this product, and changes in behaviour with nausea and vomiting during use should prompt a call to the doctor because these could be an early sign of Reye's syndrome (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings). Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if you are taking any drug for anticoagulation (thinning the blood), or for diabetes, gout or arthritis, and do not take the product if you are allergic to salicylates including aspirin or are taking other salicylate products (both OTC labels, Drug Facts, Warnings). If pregnant or breast-feeding, ask a health professional before use (both OTC labels, Drug Facts, Warnings). Keep out of reach of children; in case of overdose, get medical help or contact a Poison Control Center right away (both OTC labels, Drug Facts, Warnings). For the prescription H. pylori regimen, take the bismuth subsalicylate tablets at mealtimes and at bedtime, chew and swallow them, swallow the other tablets and capsules whole with a full glass of water, and do not double up on missed doses (prescription kit label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).
warnings: Reye's syndrome: children and teenagers who have or are recovering from chicken pox or flu-like symptoms should not use this product; when using the product, if changes in behaviour with nausea and vomiting occur, consult a doctor because these symptoms could be an early sign of Reye's syndrome, a rare but serious illness (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).

Allergy alert: contains salicylate; do not take if you are allergic to salicylates (including aspirin) or if you are taking other salicylate products (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).
Do not use if you have an ulcer, a bleeding problem, or bloody or black stool (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).

Ask a doctor before use if you have fever or mucus in the stool; ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if you are taking any drug for anticoagulation (thinning the blood), diabetes, gout or arthritis (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).

Salicylate toxicity: stop use and ask a doctor if ringing in the ears or loss of hearing occurs. Each 262.4 mg bismuth subsalicylate tablet contains an amount of salicylate comparable to approximately 130 mg aspirin, so the salicylate load, not the bismuth load, is the limiting factor in overdose (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings; prescription kit label, OVERDOSAGE).

Bismuth neurotoxicity: cases of neurotoxicity associated with excessive doses of various bismuth-containing products, including bismuth subsalicylate, have been reported; the effects have been reversible with discontinuation of therapy, and the appearance of abnormal neurologic signs and symptoms demands prompt evaluation of the benefit/risk ratio of continuation of therapy (prescription kit label, WARNINGS, Bismuth-containing products).

Gastrointestinal bleeding risk: the OTC product must not be used in patients with an ulcer or a bleeding problem, and gastrointestinal haemorrhage was reported in 1.1% of patients in the prescription kit trials (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings; prescription kit label, ADVERSE REACTIONS, Table 1).
Stop use and ask a doctor if symptoms get worse or last more than 2 days, or if diarrhoea lasts more than 2 days (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).

If pregnant or breast-feeding, ask a health professional before use; keep out of reach of children; in case of overdose, get medical help or contact a Poison Control Center right away (both OTC labels, Drug Facts, Warnings).
precautions: Darkening of the tongue and/or black stool: bismuth subsalicylate may cause a temporary and harmless darkening of the tongue and/or black stool, generally reversible within several days after treatment is stopped; stool darkening should not be confused with melena (prescription kit label, PRECAUTIONS).

Radiographic interference: bismuth absorbs x-rays and may interfere with x-ray diagnostic procedures of the gastrointestinal tract; bismuth subsalicylate may cause a temporary and harmless darkening of the stool, but this change does not interfere with standard tests for occult blood (prescription kit label, PRECAUTIONS, Laboratory Test Interactions).
Do not use in children and teenagers with chicken pox or flu-like symptoms, or in those recovering from them, because of the risk of Reye's syndrome (both OTC labels, Drug Facts, Warnings).
Self-treatment limits: use until diarrhoea stops but not more than 2 days; children under 12 years should ask a doctor before use (both OTC labels, Drug Facts, Directions).

Salicylate load: each chewable tablet of the OTC product contains salicylate 117 mg and calcium 50 mg; each 30 mL dose of the liquid contains salicylate 261 mg and magnesium 3 mg; each 525 mg caplet contains salicylate 199 mg and calcium 54 mg (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Other information; Pepto-Bismol liquid OTC label, Drug Facts, Other information; Pepto-Bismol Ultra 2x concentrated caplet OTC label, Drug Facts, Other information).

Storage: the OTC chewable tablets are to be stored at no greater than 25 degrees C and protected from excessive heat (over 40 degrees C); the liquid should be protected from freezing and kept at no greater than 25 degrees C; the prescription kit is stored at 20 to 25 degrees C (68 to 77 degrees F) (all three OTC/prescription labels, Drug Facts, Other information; prescription kit label, HOW SUPPLIED).

Missed doses in the H. pylori regimen can be made up by continuing the normal dosing schedule until the medication is gone; patients should not take double doses, and if more than 4 doses are missed the prescriber should be contacted (prescription kit label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).
serious_adverse_reactions: Salicylate poisoning, which is the principal toxicity of bismuth subsalicylate overdose: initial symptoms are hyperpnea, nausea, vomiting, tinnitus, hyperpyrexia, lethargy, tachycardia and confusion, progressing in severe cases to severe hyperpnea, convulsions, pulmonary or cerebral oedema, respiratory failure, cardiovascular collapse, coma and death (prescription kit label, OVERDOSAGE).

Bismuth neurotoxicity following excessive doses of bismuth-containing products including bismuth subsalicylate; the effects have been reversible on discontinuation of therapy (prescription kit label, WARNINGS).

Gastrointestinal haemorrhage (1.1%) and melena (3.0%) in the prescription kit trials, and the OTC contraindication in patients with an ulcer or a bleeding problem (prescription kit label, ADVERSE REACTIONS, Table 1; OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).
Tinnitus and hearing loss, which are the labelled stop-use signals for salicylate toxicity (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).

Hypersensitivity reactions to bismuth subsalicylate (urticaria, erythematous rash, flushing, fever) and to the other components of the prescription combination (prescription kit label, CONTRAINDICATIONS).
fields.pregnancy_guidance: If pregnant or breast-feeding, ask a health professional before use (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings; Pepto-Bismol liquid OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings). No letter pregnancy category is assigned in the sources used. For the prescription kit there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; the fetal toxicity and tooth-discolouration statements in that label concern the tetracycline component, and the statement specific to bismuth subsalicylate is that no reproductive toxicity studies have been conducted with bismuth subsalicylate (prescription kit label, WARNINGS and Carcinogenesis, Mutagenesis, Impairment of Fertility). No pregnancy guidance for bismuth subsalicylate appears in the WHO Model List or KEML, since neither list bismuth subsalicylate (WHO eEML 23rd List, 2023; KEML 2023).
fields.lactation_guidance: If pregnant or breast-feeding, ask a health professional before use (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings; Pepto-Bismol liquid OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings). No letter pregnancy category and no dedicated lactation section are present in the OTC labelling used. The prescription kit advises women to avoid feeding their infants with their milk during therapy, to either discontinue feeding or pump and discard milk during treatment and for 24 hours after the last dose (prescription kit label, PATIENT INFORMATION and PRECAUTIONS, Nursing Mothers); this advice arises from the metronidazole and tetracycline components. No lactation data for bismuth subsalicylate appear in the WHO Model List or KEML (WHO eEML 23rd List, 2023; KEML 2023).
fields.overdose: In case of an overdose, patients should contact a physician, poison control center, or emergency room. The main concern of an acute bismuth subsalicylate overdose focuses on the salicylate burden and not on bismuth, since less than 1% of the bismuth is normally absorbed; each 262.4 mg tablet of bismuth subsalicylate contains an amount of salicylate comparable to approximately 130 mg aspirin. Acute ingestion of less than 150 mg/kg of aspirin (i.e. less than one tablet of bismuth subsalicylate per kilogram of body weight) is not expected to lead to toxicity; mild to moderate toxicity may result from the ingestion of 150 to 300 mg/kg, while severe toxicity may occur from ingestions over 300 mg/kg. Salicylate intoxication presents a complex clinical picture, with multiple respiratory and metabolic effects resulting in fluid, electrolyte, glucose and acid-base disturbances; initial symptoms include hyperpnea, nausea, vomiting, tinnitus, hyperpyrexia, lethargy, tachycardia and confusion, and in severe cases these may progress to severe hyperpnea, convulsions, pulmonary or cerebral oedema, respiratory failure, cardiovascular collapse, coma and death (prescription kit label, OVERDOSAGE). The OTC labels simply direct the patient to get medical help or contact a Poison Control Center right away in case of overdose (both OTC labels, Drug Facts, Warnings).
fields.pharmacokinetics: Upon oral administration, bismuth subsalicylate is almost completely hydrolysed in the gastrointestinal tract to bismuth and salicylic acid. Bismuth: less than 1% of bismuth from oral doses is absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract into the systemic circulation; absorbed bismuth is distributed throughout the body and is highly bound to plasma proteins (more than 90%); bismuth has multiple disposition half-lives with an intermediate half-life of 5 to 11 days and a terminal half-life of 21 to 72 days; elimination is primarily through urinary and biliary routes with a renal clearance of 50 +/- 18 mL/min; mean trough blood bismuth concentration after 2 weeks of oral administration of 787 mg bismuth subsalicylate (3 chewable tablets) four times daily was 5.1 +/- 3.1 ng/mL, and after 525 mg (as Pepto-Bismol liquid suspension) four times daily for 2 weeks was 5 ng/mL with a highest value of 32 ng/mL. Salicylic acid: more than 80% of the salicylic acid is absorbed from oral doses of bismuth subsalicylate chewable tablets; salicylic acid is about 90% plasma protein bound; volume of distribution is about 170 mL/kg of body weight; salicylic acid is extensively metabolised and about 10% is excreted unchanged in the urine; the metabolic clearance of salicylic acid is saturable, so nonlinear pharmacokinetics are observed at bismuth subsalicylate doses above 525 mg; metabolic clearance is lower in females than in males; the terminal half-life of salicylic acid after a single oral dose of 525 mg bismuth subsalicylate is 2 to 5 hours; the mean peak plasma salicylic acid concentration after a single oral dose of 525 mg (2 chewable tablets) was 13.1 +/- 3.4 mcg/mL under fasted conditions; and the mean steady-state serum total salicylate concentration after 2 weeks of 525 mg (as Pepto-Bismol liquid suspension) four times daily was 24 mcg/mL with a highest value of 70 mcg/mL (prescription kit label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY).
clinical_pearls: Bismuth subsalicylate is a salicylate: each 262.4 mg tablet is equivalent to about 130 mg of aspirin, which is why tinnitus, hearing loss and acid-base disturbance are the toxicity to watch for rather than bismuth itself, since less than 1% of bismuth is absorbed (prescription kit label, OVERDOSAGE and CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY).
Black tongue and black stool are expected, temporary and harmless with bismuth subsalicylate, and they must not be confused with melena (prescription kit label, PRECAUTIONS).

Self-treatment is time-limited: travellers' diarrhoea or upset stomach should not be self-treated for more than 2 days, and children under 12 need a doctor's advice before use (both OTC labels, Drug Facts, Directions and Warnings).

Never confuse products: Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets contain bismuth subsalicylate 262 mg, while Pepto-Bismol liquid and Pepto-Bismol Ultra 2x concentrated caplets contain bismuth subsalicylate 525 mg per dose, and the prescription H. pylori kit uses 262.4 mg tablets dosed as 525 mg twice daily four times a day (both OTC labels and prescription kit label, DESCRIPTION/Drug Facts and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).

The classic OTC trap is self-treating a febrile or bloody diarrhoea with an antidiarrhoeal: the label says to ask a doctor before use if there is fever or mucus in the stool and not to use the product if there is bloody or black stool (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).

Reye's syndrome rules out self-medication in children and teenagers with chicken pox or influenza-like illness, and behavioural change with nausea and vomiting during use is an early sign to report (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Warnings).

Bismuth interferes with abdominal radiography because it absorbs x-rays; inform the radiology department if bismuth has recently been taken (prescription kit label, PRECAUTIONS, Laboratory Test Interactions).

Bismuth subsalicylate is not an essential medicine in the WHO Model List (23rd List, 2023) or the Kenya Essential Medicines List 2023; in the Kenyan list bismuth appears only in the context of heavy-metal poisoning (KEML 2023, footnote 76).
fields.renal_dose_adjustment: No bismuth-specific renal dose adjustment is stated in the OTC labelling. In the prescription kit, severe renal impairment is a contraindication, and this is attributed to the tetracycline component, whose antianabolic action may raise blood urea nitrogen and whose higher serum concentrations in significantly impaired renal function may lead to azotaemia, hyperphosphataemia and acidosis (prescription kit label, CONTRAINDICATIONS). For bismuth itself, elimination is primarily urinary and biliary with a renal clearance of 50 +/- 18 mL/min, and bismuth has an intermediate half-life of 5 to 11 days and a terminal half-life of 21 to 72 days (prescription kit label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY); there is no labelled renal dose adjustment for bismuth subsalicylate.
fields.administration_instructions: OTC Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets: fully chew before swallowing; adults and children 12 years and over take 2 chewable tablets every half hour or 4 every hour as needed for diarrhoea and 2 every half hour to 1 hour as needed for overindulgence, not exceeding 8 doses (16 tablets) in 24 hours, and use until diarrhoea stops but not more than 2 days; children under 12 years should ask a doctor; each chewable tablet contains calcium 50 mg and salicylate 117 mg; store at no greater than 25 degrees C and avoid excessive heat (over 40 degrees C) (Pepto-Bismol chewable tablets OTC label, Drug Facts, Directions and Other information). OTC Pepto-Bismol liquid: shake well before use and use only the dose cup provided; 30 mL every half hour or 60 mL every hour as needed for diarrhoea, and 30 mL every half hour as needed for overindulgence, not exceeding 8 doses (240 mL) in 24 hours; each 30 mL dose contains magnesium 3 mg, sodium 4 mg and salicylate 261 mg; protect from freezing and store at no greater than 25 degrees C (Pepto-Bismol liquid OTC label, Drug Facts, Directions and Other information). Prescription H. pylori regimen: the bismuth subsalicylate tablets are chewed and swallowed, the metronidazole tablet and tetracycline capsule are swallowed whole with a full glass of water (8 ounces), the medicines are taken at mealtimes and at bedtime, adequate fluid intake is recommended particularly with the bedtime dose of tetracycline to reduce the risk of oesophageal irritation and ulceration, and the product is stored at 20 to 25 degrees C (68 to 77 degrees F) (prescription kit label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION and HOW SUPPLIED).

notes: The table stores this agent as 'Bismuth Subsalicylate' with drug_class 'Gastrointestinal agent' and brand_names ['Bismuth']; the previous row carried shared class-template gastrointestinal text, which is superseded by this draft. Bismuth subsalicylate is an over-the-counter antacid/antidiarrhoeal in the United States and has no FDA prescription label of its own, so the monograph combines three evidence streams: (1) the FDA/DailyMed OTC Drug Facts labels for the actual Pepto-Bismol products - chewable tablets (bismuth subsalicylate 262 mg per tablet, salicylate 117 mg, calcium 50 mg), the liquid suspension (bismuth subsalicylate 525 mg per 30 mL, salicylate 261 mg) and the Ultra 2x concentrated caplets (525 mg, salicylate 199 mg) - used for indications, directions, warnings, contraindications-as-prohibitions and administration; (2) the FDA prescription label for the Bismuth Subsalicylate Chewable Tablets/Metronidazole Tablets/Tetracycline Hydrochloride Capsules kit (Ailex Pharmaceuticals), which is the only FDA prescription label text that contains bismuth subsalicylate-specific pharmacology: the description of bismuth subsalicylate as a highly insoluble salt of trivalent bismuth and salicylic acid, the hydrolysis to bismuth and salicylic acid, the full bismuth and salicylic acid pharmacokinetics, the salicylate-dose equivalence of one 262.4 mg tablet to about 130 mg aspirin, the overdose spectrum, the reversible bismuth neurotoxicity warning, the black tongue/black stool precaution, the x-ray interference precaution, the bismuth-specific interaction statements (anticoagulants, aspirin, antidiabetic agents, probenecid/sulfinpyrazone) and the 14-day H. pylori regimen; every statement in this draft that derives from the other two components of that kit (metronidazole and tetracycline) is explicitly flagged as such in the field text; and (3) the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines, 23rd List (2023) and the Kenya Essential Medicines List 2023, both checked and both confirmed NOT to list bismuth subsalicylate, which is stated in the indications field rather than left as a silent omission. Product differentiation note: the Pepto-Bismol-branded products sourced here contain bismuth subsalicylate only; Pepto-Bismol Maximum Strength, which is a brand variant that contains acetaminophen as well as bismuth subsalicylate, has no DailyMed listing and no retrievable FDA label text, so it is deliberately excluded from every field and listed under unsourced_fields rather than being described from memory. Bismuth subsalicylate is not an essential medicine in either the WHO Model List or KEML 2023; in the Kenyan list bismuth appears only in the context of heavy-metal poisoning (footnote 76).
